opening: These are the last backlog entries no walkthrough has shown you: 30 suspected bugs and 38 wishlist and deferred-run entries from Archive Suite and Vision OCR. Each wishlist entry was checked against the code today, so the sheet says what is already built.
intro: The entries are every open entry of the registered backlog files (Agent Manager backlogs.json) not yet marked seen on 2026-11-20. Suspected bugs are from verification/SUSPECTS.md, grouped by app and by what would go wrong. Wishlist entries were checked against the code by a read-only pass the same day. Entries an earlier call of yours settles are in the last section, answered by that call unless you reopen one.
excluded: The Agent Manager's 27 entries: engineering housekeeping, settled by the session on 2026-11-20 (12 closed as built or fixed, 14 accepted, 1 queued) under your rule of 2026-11-19.

Two code-tidying entries, settled by the session as housekeeping: shared finalize and organize helpers in the Processor (the block is still copied four times on a file-moving path, so it is queued behind nice-to-have with a review), and the retag call sites (closed above).
Entries walked with you earlier today or in earlier walkthroughs.

items.title: Processor: nine suspected bugs that could file or tag documents wrongly, with no warning
items.what: Each of these, if real, writes something wrong into a user's filed PDFs or tags, or leaves work out, and says nothing. These paths have no undo.
list: S-028 · A chosen folder is read one level deep: photos in sub-folders of a box are silently left out.
S-034 · With collection segmentation on, "No tagging" and "Copy source tags" still write Box and Folder tags, replacing the copied tags.
S-036 · A collection name edited in the review sheet is used exactly as typed: a "/" stops filing part-way, ".." files outside the output folder.
S-035 · Resuming a batch files documents without the per-page review and the box/folder confirmation.
S-042 · When the tagging call fails, the document is filed with no subjects or date, and the run still reports it tagged.
S-033 · A model reply with no year and no "uncertain" flag gives a document no date tags at all, not even Date Uncertain.
S-031 · Under a window segmentation approach, a letter's enclosure may not get the letter's date.
S-017 · On already-OCRed input, the "review document segmentation" step is skipped even when it is turned on.
S-040 · A year typed on the phone is combined with the day and month the OCR read from a different date.
items.rec_why: These touch irreversible paths in what users file, which is where a bug costs most, and each check is a small scratch-folder test.

items.title: Processor: five suspected bugs that make users pay more than they expect
items.what: Each of these, if real, spends a user's API money twice, for nothing, or beyond the estimate shown.
list: S-039 · "Stage for later" can hand the same photos to Process Files twice, so they are read and paid for twice.
S-032 · A segmentation approach with no key can be started; the run reads every page, then fails after the reading is paid for.
S-041 · The cost estimate leaves out the dating and item-field calls, about half the calls in a measured run.
S-026 · Batch reading sends large scans at full size, so batch runs cost more than the estimate.
S-027 · Batch mode is offered for providers that have no batch; the run goes standard but the panes show the batch price, and turning it on still switches off other features.
items.rec_why: Wrong spending is the kind of bug a user notices on their bill, and each is checkable on scratch with the $0 stand-in.

S-018 · The app says it paces to the subscription window and retries, but the reading step does not pace.

S-030 · The run log can give one failed file another file's reason when two share a name.

items.title: Phone over the Drive relay: two suspected bugs
items.what: The Drive relay carries photos from the phone to the Mac through Google Drive when they are not on the same network.
list: S-021 · Android reports a segment as sent when the Drive write failed, so the Mac shows no tag card for it until Finish.

items.title: Notes: six smaller suspected bugs
items.what: Each of these, if real, is an annoyance or a misleading result rather than lost work.
list: S-012 · The tag filter finds nothing unless the tag is typed with the capitals it was stored with ("intel" misses "Intel").
S-016 · Clicking a column header in the notes list moves the sort arrow but may not re-sort the list.
S-010 · Removing several notes from a folder at once asks about only the last one; the others quietly stay.
S-011 · "New from Template" from a row's menu can miss the template's last second of edits.
S-014 · If the archive folder is moved or its drive ejected while Notes runs, links report "Source file not found" instead of asking to find it.
S-008 · A window resized just before quitting may reopen at its old size.

items.what: A check of the code today found each of these done, or its premise gone.
list: Handwriting recognition mode (Processor): built. Handwritten pages go to the handwriting reader, and "Read handwriting on typed pages" is on by default since call 24.
Newspaper and periodical layouts (Processor): built. Newspaper pages are read region by region with the layout detector.
Collection-level metadata (Processor): built as the containers work (repository, collection, series, box, folder), approved by you on 21 Oct.
First-run wizard, forced or dismissible (Processor): settled in the shipped app. It is dismissible, with "Skip: free, on this Mac", and reopens from Settings.
Provider caveats in the app's text (Processor): built. The EU/UK/Switzerland paid-tier warning and the free-tier training notes are in the key wizard and Settings.
Smaller code de-duplications (Processor): the remainder shipped on 26 Sep.
Box and folder colour retagging, three drifted copies (Processor): the drift is fixed; all three use one shared rule. Three short call sites remain, which is harmless.
One page-2 header builder across the apps (Notes): no longer true. Only the Processor builds that header; the Reader and Notes only read it through the shared package.
items.rec_why: Leaving built work on a wishlist makes the lists unreadable, which is what W49.potential-features-tidy was filed to fix.

items.title: Five early ideas from July, recommended to drop
items.what: These were written before the app took its present shape. None has been asked for since.
list: Spreading a large job across several API keys for speed: providers treat this as getting round their rate limits, and it can breach their terms.
Streaming batch results instead of holding them in memory: no memory problem has been measured; the PDF writer's memory is its own item (W49.proc-pdfa-memory).
A plugin system for custom classification and tagging: a large build for developers, not for the archive users the app is for.
A headless REST server mode: the same; the only server today is Live Capture's pairing link.
Accuracy metrics against the user's own ground truth: users will not have truth files; the bench measures this for the app, and Tools ▸ Compare Models shows readers side by side.
items.rec_why: Each is a large build that serves developers or a problem nobody has seen.

items.title: Language detection on the built-in Apple Vision route
items.what: The Processor's Apple Vision reader uses a language list the user picks and does not detect the language. The Vision engine it already includes (VisionOCRKit) detects the language itself when the list is left empty, but the Processor's own Vision client does not use that. The cloud and local model readers handle languages without a setting.
items.now: Small [S]: let the Vision route detect the language when the user has not chosen one, and measure it on the bench's non-English pages.
items.rec_why: A user with French or German papers on the free on-device route gets worse reading today for want of a setting they may never find.

items.title: Export tables as structured data (CSV)
items.what: Pages of kind "Form or table" are detected and read by the forms reader, but the result is text, not a table. This would export a table's rows and columns as CSV for a spreadsheet.
items.now: Cell-level reading is still bench work (W46.ocr-cells-l4-more, behind nice-to-have, which waits on cell truth you said you could not rule).
items.rec_why: It depends on cell reading that is not yet measured well enough to trust.

items.title: Subject tags informed by nearby documents
items.what: The tagger already sees up to three neighbouring documents, but uses them only to estimate dates. This would let neighbours inform the subject tags too, for example a letter whose subject is clear only from the reply next to it.
items.now: Nothing measures whether it would help; it would need a bench comparison before any build.
items.rec_why: It could as easily spread one document's subjects onto its neighbours, and nothing suggests the current tags are short of context.
items.where: ArchiveProcessor/POTENTIAL_FEATURES.md "Tag suggestions from nearby documents"; Tagging/TagGenerator.swift

items.title: Apple Shortcuts actions
items.what: Expose actions such as "process this folder" to the Shortcuts app, so users can automate them. Nothing like it exists in any of the three apps.
items.rec_why: A modest build that only a few users would use; worth doing once the apps are public and someone asks.

items.title: Tropy integration in the Reader
items.what: Tropy is a free desktop tool historians use to organise research photos. The Zotero half of this entry has shipped (Export to Zotero and Add to Zotero); nothing exists for Tropy.
items.rec_why: Zotero covers the common case; Tropy users are a smaller group and nobody has asked.

items.title: Zotero links that open a PDF at a page
items.what: Notes links to Zotero items with zotero://select, which shows the item. Zotero also supports zotero://open-pdf, which opens the attachment at a given page, so a citation could jump straight to the page quoted.
items.rec_why: A small, useful step for Zotero users, but nothing depends on it.

items.title: Stable block identities and "extracts made from this note"
items.what: Extracts point at a passage by its position in the source note. Giving each block a permanent identity would let Notes show, on a note, how many extracts were made from it, and keep an extract's link firm if the source is rearranged.
items.rec_why: Extracts are snapshots by design (you declined refreshing them today), so a firmer link matters less.

items.title: Scrolling within a merged PDF from a source preview
items.what: Clicking a source block shows the cited page alone. In a PDF that merges several documents, this would let the preview scroll to neighbouring pages.
items.rec_why: Opening the source in the Reader already gives the whole PDF.

items.title: Publish the bench results page publicly
items.what: The page of measured OCR, segmentation and handwriting results is published today as a private artifact. This would put it on GitHub Pages with a public link, next to the public repository.
items.now: The page shows scores on your own 96 pages, though not the pages themselves.
items.rec_why: It is most useful beside a public release of the apps, which has not happened yet; nothing is lost by waiting.

items.title: A visible-text mode for debugging the searchable text layer
items.what: Make the invisible text layer of a searchable PDF visible, to check where words sit. The file itself argues against it: two probe tools already measure that numerically, and a visible-text setting is one users would find and turn on by accident.
items.rec_why: As the file says. Vision OCR is merging into the Processor, so the answer carries over.

items.title: How the Mac apps reach other users
items.what: Today the apps are signed with a self-made certificate and not notarized, so a new user has to go to Privacy & Security and press Open Anyway, and no public release is posted. The two routes to a normal install both need Apple's Developer Program ($99 a year): a notarized download from GitHub Releases, or the Mac App Store.
items.now: No decision of yours is recorded; the wishlist marks it undecided. Enrolling is real money over the $7 rule, so it comes back to you before anything is paid.
items.rec_why: The App Store's sandbox would forbid things the Processor does today, such as running the Claude and ChatGPT command-line tools for the plan routes, so a notarized download keeps the app as it is.

choices.defer: Keep store publishing deferred until the Mac release route is settled
choices.plan: Plan it now as part of the first public release

items.title: Publishing the phone companions to the App Store and Google Play
items.what: Five entries describe the steps: the Apple programme ($99 a year) and a Google Play account ($25 once); store screenshots; Google's rule that a new account runs a closed test with 12 testers for 14 days first; and Apple's rule against apps that do nothing alone, so the listing must say the companion needs the Mac app (its connect screen already says so). Without the stores, users can install the Android app from a file but not the iPhone app.
list: Apple: enrol, App ID and certificates, test on a real iPhone, upload, privacy form, review.
Google: Play Console account, sign the app bundle, data-safety form, submit.
Store screenshots and a short recording of each companion (only you can make these on a device).
Play's closed test: 12 testers for 14 days before production.
Apple's "minimal functionality" risk: the listing and first run must state the Mac dependency.
items.rec_why: The steps follow from the Mac release decision and the real-iPhone pass (W40.i4), neither of which is done.
